planting_details.assumptions_or_notes: Assumes rainfed smallholder maize in Kitale during the long rains of 2010. H614 is a highland hybrid commonly used in this zone. PPOP=4.8 plants/m² with PLRS=75 cm implies ~28 cm within-row spacing, matching local recommendations (1 plant per hill). Planting depth 5 cm assumes moist loam soils; deeper or shallower adjustments may be made for soil moisture. Row direction set to 0 (N–S) as no field-specific constraint provided; many farmers follow contours for erosion control, which could differ.

events.Assumptions_or_Notes: Basal DAP (18-46-0) placed in the planting hole, banded beneath surface (~5 cm). Rate chosen to supply 22.5 kg N/ha via ~125 kg DAP/ha (0.18 N fraction). P as elemental calculated from P2O5 using 0.46 × 0.4364 = 0.2007; thus 125 × 0.46 × 0.4364 ≈ 25.1 kg P/ha. This reflects common local practice to use DAP at planting; exact amount adjusted to help reach the required total N while keeping practice realistic.

Topdress CAN (26% N) once at ~28 DAP, banded on the soil surface in a ring around plants (common smallholder practice), not incorporated; relies on rainfall for incorporation. 67.5 kg N/ha corresponds to ~260 kg CAN/ha (67.5/0.26). Timing matches typical Western Kenya topdress window (3–5 weeks after emergence). Rate is higher than average farmer norms but is set to meet the experiment’s exact total N=90 kg/ha while preserving locally typical product, timing, and placement.
